summary: Monika Boehm-Tettelbach is an Indologist, linguist, and religious studies scholar. She earned her doctorate at the Free University of Berlin under Heinz-Jürgen Pinnow and completed her Habilitation at the University of Bonn, later holding professorships at Bonn, Cologne, Bamberg, and Heidelberg.
Monika Nowakowska is a scholar in the fields of Indology and philosophy, affiliated with the University of Warsaw (attested 2010 and 2026).

Monika Zin works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology. She studied at Jagiellonian University, the Academy of Fine Arts Vienna, and the University of Munich. She held professorships at Munich and the Free University of Berlin and posts at Leipzig and the Saxon Academy.
Moodeen Sheriff was an Indologist and medical professional who studied at Madras Medical College and served as Native Surgeon at the Triplicane Dispensary from 1858 to 1889.

Moriichi Yamazaki is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Tohoku University and Cambridge under K. R. Norman. He served as professor at Sendai National College of Technology (~1985–2003) and president of Hosen Gakuen College (~2003–2010).

Moritz Abraham Stern worked in linguistics and mathematics. He studied at Heidelberg University and the University of Göttingen under Carl Friedrich Gauss and Karl Otfried Müller, subsequently serving as Extraordinarius at Göttingen from 1829 to 1884.

Moriz Haupt was a scholar of linguistics and classical literature who studied under Gottfried Hermann at the University of Leipzig. He held professorships at Leipzig (1841–1851) and Humboldt University of Berlin (from 1853), and served as perpetual secretary of the Prussian Academy.

Moriz Winternitz was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Vienna under Georg Bühler and under Max Müller. He held academic posts at Oxford, Charles University, and Visva-Bharati University, and was professor at the German University Prague.

Morten Schlütter is a Buddhist studies scholar and sinologist. He studied at Copenhagen, Komazawa, and Yale under Stanley Weinstein, and held teaching posts at Victoria University of Wellington, UCLA, Wisconsin-Madison, and the University of Iowa.

Mortimer Wheeler was an archaeologist who studied at UCL under A. E. Housman and at the University of London. He was director of the National Museum of Wales and London Museum, and Director-General of Archæology in India (1944–1948).

Morton Klass was a scholar in religious studies, Indology, and anthropology. He studied at Brooklyn College and Columbia University, where he earned his doctorate, and later held posts at Bennington College, Barnard College, and Columbia University.
Mother Sayamagyi was a teacher and practitioner in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied under and succeeded Sayagyi U Ba Khin, and later taught Roger Bischoff.

Motohiro Yoritomi was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University under Gadjin Nagao and Yuichi Kajiyama. He served as professor at Shuchiin University and the Graduate University for Advanced Studies.

Motoi Ono is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied under Yasunori Ejima at the University of Tsukuba and earned his doctorate at the University of Vienna, later serving as associate professor at the University of Tsukuba.
Moumita Hossain is an Indology and archaeology scholar who studied under Ranjit Sen and is affiliated with The Asiatic Society as a research scholar and fellow (attested 2026).

Mrinalkanti Gangopadhyaya is a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He served as a professor at Vidyasagar College (attested 1970–1975) and taught in the Department of Sanskrit at the University of Calcutta (attested 1982, 1994).

Mudagamuwe Maithrimurthi is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen and held positions at Leipzig, Heidelberg, and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.
Muhamad Saputra is a PhD student at the Australian National University studying under the supervision of Assa Doron (attested 2026).

Muhammad Ashraf Khan is a scholar in archaeology and Buddhist studies. He held posts as Deputy Director at the Taxila Museum and Director at both the Department of Archaeology and Museums, Andhra Pradesh, and Quaid-i-Azam University.

Muhammad Nasim Khan is an archaeologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and linguist. He earned an M.Phil at the University of Peshawar, where he became an assistant professor, and held visiting posts at Hamburg and the Royal Asiatic Society.
